originalTitle: Anduril now says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch

content: On Tuesday, defense contractor Anduril and chipmaker Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, starting with a single model in 2027. They also announced a “long-term goal” of pushing the computer industry to create “a fully domestic supply chain.” Even a single Made-in-USA laptop would be a surprise, because no major US computer company builds its laptops here — not Apple, not Dell, not HP, not Microsoft. We’re not aware of any company that does. But we are aware of companies that have briefly and strategically assembled computers here seemingly to appease President Donald Trump. We’re also aware of companies that have promised US jobs only to deliver empty buildings. And we’re aware of at least one fake “US” company that lied to the government about making product domestically. That’s why we now ask pointed questions when a company says it’s committed to US manufacturing. We asked TP-Link those sorts of questions just over a week ago. On Monday, we asked Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Qualcomm president and CEO Cristiano Amon those kinds of questions. Over the course of two days, Anduril has changed one important answer. Anduril communications VP Shannon Prior now says the company’s laptop will have at least 65 percent of its components made in the US by the time it launches in 2027. It’s an important number, and one that Anduril did not commit to earlier this week. Luckey held a call with reporters on Monday, during which he was clear that he wants to make literally every part of a computer in the United States — and that Anduril and Qualcomm have already mapped out a plan. “We have a technical roadmap to get to 100 percent domestic over time,” he told journalists. Luckey also suggested his laptop would be built to comply with the requirements of the military and other government agencies — and that it would meet or exceed one specific US government standard that has an exact definition. “We are not just barely meeting the bar for Made in America. We are going hard to make this an all-American play, and not even the Buy American Act requires what we’re trying,” Luckey said. The Buy American Act dates back to 1933, but it was updated during the Biden Administration to require that at least 65 percent of the cost of a company’s products must be made domestically for it be considered a domestic product itself. That number is going up to 75 percent in 2029. Many products need to be made in America to those standards, or federal agencies can’t buy them without receiving a waiver — which agencies currently use en masse, Luckey himself argued on the call. “There’s a number of government agencies that are required by law to buy American-made computers [...] All of those procurements are happening under waivers of those laws,” he said. We also noticed that Anduril’s press release specifies that its first laptop will be “designed and assembled” in the United States, not necessarily “manufactured” here (though the release does talk about future manufacturing). This was also a sticking point with router maker TP-Link, which would not confirm full manufacturing even after suggesting it in an interview with The Verge. That’s why we asked Luckey what percent of his first laptop’s components would be made in the US. His reply was not 65 percent or 70 percent. It was “TBD.” You can read the exchange for yourself: > The Verge: When it arrives in 2027, what percent of the components in the BlueChip laptop will be made in the US? > Luckey: TBD. I’m doing my very, very best. It’s gonna be a whole mix of things based on when do certain memory fabs come online? When do certain CPU, GPU fabs come online? There’s a whole— Like, am I able to get a display line here or not? Do I have to do that after launch? I’m being totally open kimono with you here. Those questions are not settled. It is not clear if I will be able. I know the glass is gonna be made in the US, I know the frame is gonna be made in the US around that display. I know that parts of the ribbon component are gonna be made in the U.S. I don’t know if I will have successfully pulled that component in or a dozen other components. So it’s a little up in the air. I’m doing my very, very best. I think most likely the thing that we ship is not going to be 100-percent American. I think it’ll be a blend of US and allies around the world, mostly US, probably a few things from some allies, and then that’ll be in the context of conversations with those allies about bringing those components into production in the United States, and I’m being honest with the government on this too. I mean, I’ve had conversations where I’ve said, listen. I would love to give you guys an American, 100-percent American laptop right off the bat, but that is not the environment the US government has created or US industry has created. I can’t let the perfect be the enemy of the good. When we followed up by email to ask specifically about 65 percent, the answer was that the laptop prototype is currently at 32 percent and Anduril could not yet commit to 65 percent. Here’s Anduril spokesperson Stephanie Davis’ full reply on Tuesday: > For the prototype today, approximately 32% is U.S.-origin by component procurement cost, and more than 90% is sourced from the United States and allied countries combined. > We’re working to expand domestic sourcing and production ahead of planned availability in 2027, with the goal of eliminating foreign content and ultimately establishing an end-to-end American supply chain. > The final domestic-content percentage at launch remains unsettled, so we can’t confirm above or below 65% today. That’s why we’re asking you to revise the assertion that it will be “well below” that threshold. Today, Prior writes that Anduril can indeed commit to 65 percent. chineseContent: 周二，国防承包商 Anduril 和芯片制造商高通宣布建立合作伙伴关系，从 2027 年开始，完全在美国生产笔记本电脑。他们还宣布了推动计算机行业创建“完全国内供应链”的“长期目标”。即使是一台美国制造的笔记本电脑也会让人感到惊讶，因为没有一家美国大型计算机公司在这里生产笔记本电脑——苹果、戴尔、惠普、微软都没有。我们不知道有哪家公司这样做。但我们知道有些公司在这里进行了短暂而战略性的计算机组装，似乎是为了安抚唐纳德·特朗普总统。我们还知道，有些公司承诺为美国提供就业机会，但结果却是空置的建筑。我们知道至少有一家假“美国”公司就在国内生产产品向政府撒谎。这就是为什么当一家公司表示致力于美国制造业时，我们现在会提出尖锐的问题。就在一周前，我们向 TP-Link 询问了此类问题。周一，我们向 Anduril 创始人 Palmer Luckey 和高通总裁兼首席执行官 Cristiano Amon 提出了此类问题。两天的时间里，安杜里尔改变了一个重要的答案。 Anduril 通信副总裁 Shannon Prior 现在表示，到 2027 年推出时，该公司的笔记本电脑至少 65% 的零部件将在美国制造。这是一个重要的数字，Anduril 本周早些时候没有承诺这一数字。拉基周一与记者举行了电话会议，期间他明确表示，他希望在美国生产计算机的所有部件，而且安杜里尔和高通已经制定了计划。 “我们有一个技术路线图，随着时间的推移，将实现 100% 国内化，”他告诉记者。 Luckey 还建议他的笔记本电脑将符合
